summary: Parliament's Finance Committee reviewed pay and benefits that Parliament sets under Article 102 of the Constitution. It found gaps: the Speaker was paid less than the Deputy Speaker and ordinary MPs, ministers got smaller car benefits than lower-ranked posts, and island councillors earned far less than city councillors and some council staff. It proposed a special allowance for the Speaker, bigger car benefits for Cabinet ministers and a new service allowance for island councillors.
keyPoints: Speaker gets a MVR 22,000 special allowance, taking total monthly pay from MVR 73,125 to MVR 95,125 (Deputy Speaker gets MVR 91,000, MPs MVR 82,500)
Cabinet ministers' car benefits rise from MVR 7,500 to MVR 17,000 a month (petrol, driver salary and driver living allowance), about MVR 1.71 million more a year for 15 ministers
All 626 island council presidents, vice presidents and members get a MVR 5,000 monthly service allowance, about MVR 37.56 million more a year
Changes take effect from the day Parliament passes the report; the committee decided by majority at its 24th meeting on 21 October 2026
outcome: Passed by Parliament on 28 October 2026 (42 yes, 12 no)
